name: Waseda
tagline: Otemachi in 11 minutes and Shinjuku in 15 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥90,000 to ¥100,000.
summary: The station is in Shinjuku City, where Tokyo Metro run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 11 minutes to Otemachi, 15 minutes to Shinjuku, 24 minutes to Shibuya and 32 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. The station stands 14.8 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 19.2 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 14.8 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 5.9 m to 25.1 m, a difference of 19.2 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Even so, 3 of the nine points within 400 m fall inside the area, and the deepest projection there is 0.5 to 3 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 7 clinics and 18 pharmacies. The nearest hospital is 国立国際医療センター, about 9 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 神経研究所附属晴和病院, about 11 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyo Metro Tozai Line.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Tozai Line runs at 160% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 木場→門前仲町, which this station is not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥90,000 to ¥100,000 and 1K ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. 1LDK ¥190,000 to ¥200,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

neighbours.lead: For what it offers families, Waseda (Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line)); for how close the centre is, Waseda.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Waseda. Waseda adds the Tokyo Metro Tozai Line; Waseda (Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line)) adds the Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line). Waseda is at least 23 minutes quicker to Otemachi and Tokyo. On what it offers families, though, Waseda (Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line)) comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: For quiet, Ushigome-Yanagicho; for lower rent, Waseda.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Waseda. Waseda adds the Tokyo Metro Tozai Line; Ushigome-Yanagicho adds the Toei Oedo Line. Which is faster depends on where you are going: Waseda is 6 minutes quicker to Shinagawa, Ushigome-Yanagicho is 10 minutes quicker to Roppongi. A one-room flat costs about ¥17,000 more at Ushigome-Yanagicho. On quiet, Ushigome-Yanagicho comes out ahead.

leads.terrain: There are gentle slopes around the station, and which block you live on changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 10 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 1 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself is outside the projected flood area, but blocks nearby are inside it.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyo Metro Tozai Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
